role: Dual-source time verification — compares local system time against an external time source and recommends Fortress Mode (default-deny lockdown posture) when drift exceeds a threshold or the external source is unreachable at all.
behaviorDescription: verifyTemporalIntegrity() compares a local timestamp against an external one (or null if unreachable) and flags a recommendation for Fortress Mode if drift exceeds a configurable threshold (default 500ms) OR the external source could not be reached at all — an unreachable source is treated exactly as seriously as detected drift, per the default-deny principle. Deliberately does not flip any global process-wide switch itself, since nothing in this repo currently reads such a switch — this bot detects and recommends, it does not unilaterally enact a lockdown. Classified Synchronous Gate: a genuine temporal integrity failure requires an explicit human verdict (via the Policy Arbitrator's recordVerdict()) before anything depending on trusted time proceeds. fetchExternalTime() is an honest stub: it throws a clear error, because this environment has no network access to verify a real HTTPS call to an external time source.
hardStops: Never flips a global Fortress Mode switch itself — detects and recommends only, a human decides via the Synchronous Gate
Treats an unreachable external time source exactly as seriously as detected drift — never treats 'could not check' as 'assume fine'
fetchExternalTime() never fakes a network response — it throws until a real, verifiable network call exists
